name: Is my PDF uploaded anywhere to convert it?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The text is read and structured into Markdown entirely in your browser using pdf.js. Your PDF never leaves your device.

name: Does PDFree store or log my files after processing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. PDFree runs entirely in your browser — there is no backend server that receives your files. Because nothing is uploaded, nothing can be stored, logged, or retained. Your document exists only in your browser's memory for the duration of the session and is cleared when you close the tab.

name: Does it preserve tables and images?

acceptedAnswer.text: Simple tables are detected automatically and converted to Markdown table syntax. Images/figures are extracted too — the download becomes a .zip (document.md + an images folder) whenever the PDF has extractable images, or a plain .md when it doesn't. If you need more reliable table extraction, use PDF to Excel; for a fully editable document, use PDF to Word.
PDFree compares each line's font size to the document's typical body-text size. Noticeably larger text becomes a Markdown heading (#, ##, or ### depending on how much larger).

name: What kinds of lists are recognized?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bulleted lines (•, ◦, ▪ and similar markers) and numbered lines ("1.", "2)") are converted to Markdown list syntax. Letter or roman-numeral lists (a., iv.) are left as plain text, since those markers are too easy to confuse with real content.

name: Is this a free PDF to Markdown converter with no sign up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. PDFree is completely free — no sign up, no account, no installation. Open the tool, load your PDF, and download the .md file.
Only if the PDF already has a text layer. Scanned, image-only PDFs have no extractable text — run OCR PDF first, then convert the result.

name: Is this good for preparing PDFs for AI tools, RAG, or LLM context?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — Markdown is a common, lightweight format for feeding documents into an LLM's context window or a RAG pipeline, and converting locally means the document's content never has to leave your device just to reformat it. Table detection is heuristic-based, so complex or densely formatted tables may still lose some structure — for table-heavy documents, check the output before feeding it to a model, or run OCR first if the PDF is scanned.
